articles.title: Your home organization can actually look stylish. These 27 designer-approved solutions are proof
articles.summary: If you feel like you’re drowning in stuff and can’t find anything you need, there’s a box (or basket) for that. 11 products our writers rely on to organize and declutter. Sign up for the Filter US newsletter, your weekly guide to buying fewer, better things.
body: Look around your house and be honest: are you drowning in stuff? I know I am. Between a toddler, one on the way, two cats and a personal inability to throw out junk “just in case”, it’s rare I see the actual surface of my floor or countertops.

Without a home organization system that works for you, the sheer amount of objects you have accumulated throughout the years can quickly overrun your home. Many of us tend to put away stuff “for now”, only for our closets and cabinets to fill up, preventing us from seeing what we own. “If you can’t find something, it can feel easier to order another one than to spend 20 minutes searching,” Amy Berryhill, a professional organizer and owner of Spiffy Chicks, said.

The best way to make space for everything you need is to make intentional – and stylish! – choices about how you organize your home. “We like to think about organization as an extension of the design process, finding ways to give everyday items a designated home without sacrificing beauty,” said Audrey Scheck, an interior designer and founder of Audrey Scheck Design.

articles.title: Gloria Steinem obituary
articles.summary: Unflinching campaigner for women’s and civil rights who galvanised a generation of activists. Gloria Steinem, who has died aged 92, was a writer, community organiser, political campaigner and a charismatic feminist activist who called herself “an entrepreneur of social change”.
body: Steinem, unlike some of her contemporaries, never recanted or modified her many causes, which included civil rights, violence against women, and the struggle for equality. She continued to argue that every economics course ought to start not with production but with reproduction, and an understanding of the patriarchal instinct to restrict a woman’s right to contraception and abortion.

She was one of Donald Trump’s most outspoken critics throughout his rise to power. She labelled him “harasser in chief”, a man whose rhetoric and conduct ran counter to the values she had dedicated her life to advocating.

In 1963, when Betty Friedan published The Feminine Mystique – describing the frustration of affluent, well-educated, middle-class white women trapped in domesticity – Steinem was “a girl reporter” living in New York, working on The Beach Book, a compendium of extracts from literature about beaches and tips on what to do in the sun. A rising media star who was later described, to her annoyance, as “the world’s most beautiful byline”, she had already begun to make connections: she asked the economist JK Galbraith to write the foreword, and he agreed.
points: Unflinching campaigner for women’s and civil rights who galvanised a generation of activists.

articles.title: My dad died suddenly with no will. Am I morally obliged to share his estate with my estranged half-sibling? | Leading questions
articles.summary: It’s kind of you to wonder if you should change the way things were left, writes advice columnist Eleanor Gordon-Smith. But it’s possible his preference is already clear. My dad died suddenly earlier this year, with no will, and I am unsure as to how I should distribute the estate.
body: My dad was a very ethical person. While his death was unexpected, he had a sense it was coming. Around six months before he died, he arranged for the disposal of many personal effects. The lack of a will, given his self-discipline and preferences for forward planning, is odd.

My dad has two daughters from a previous relationship, who he was not in contact with until I was in my mid-30s. Their mum had remarried after separating from our dad, and her new husband had formally adopted both her girls. My dad was delighted to resume contact with one half-sister. Another, two years younger, wanted nothing to do with him and firmly disapproved of her sister’s choice to re-establish contact.

Some 10 years ago, I started my own family, relocated to remove myself from domestic abuse, and joined the league of parents of children with additional needs. My dad mentioned that he had a little money put aside that could go towards legal costs, should courts ever become involved in arrangements for my son.
points: It’s kind of you to wonder if you should change the way things were left, writes advice columnist Eleanor Gordon-Smith.
But it’s possible his preference is already clear.

articles.title: The Best Liquid Blushes That Offer a Natural, Skin-Like Flush
articles.summary: In search of a rosy cheek? Three traits define the best liquid blush: buildable, lightweight, and long-wearing. We included options from Saie, Armani Beauty, and more.
body: Not so long ago, blush played a supporting role—the step you skipped when running late, a swipe of powder somewhere near the cheekbone, if that. Too much, too rosy, too eighties. Then it came back with a vengeance: worn higher on the face, in brighter shades, in placements that a decade ago you might’ve deemed a mistake (blush blindness, we’ve all been there). The format leading the return is liquid: It melts into skin, builds a dot at a time, blends with a fingertip, and reads like a natural flush rather than ‘makeup’.

The formulas have caught up, too. Early liquid blushes could be unforgiving—“either extremely pigmented, difficult to blend, or so emollient that they disrupted the complexion underneath,” Jaikaran says. “This is where the term ‘blush blindness’ came from.” The new generation gives you more playtime to blend and sets down better. Wear time has stretched to what Spickard describes as formulas “that almost stain” and ingredients now read like serums and include skin-loving factors like hyaluronic acid, niacinamide, ceramides, peptides, and more. Even the delivery system keeps evolving, from mousses and gels to tints.
points: Three traits define the best liquid blush: buildable, lightweight, and long-wearing.

articles.title: Should You Travel to Nepal Right Now? What Locals Want International Travelers to Know
articles.summary: Whether you have travel planned, or are considering booking a trip, here's what experts on the ground say.
body: I arrive in Kathmandu on the last day of August, just five days after devastating flash floods —caused by a glacier and rock collapse along Nepal’s border with China—swept through the Rasuwa district. Entire villages and communities were wiped out, hundreds killed, and thousands more are still missing, including many tourists. It’s an unthinkable tragedy that has unfolded with devastating consequences across parts of Nepal and neighboring Tibet.

As I exit baggage claim at Tribhuvan International Airport, one of a tiny handful of non-Nepalis on my flight from Dubai, I see a Flood Related Information & Help Desk manned by police. Outside the airport, the streets are busy, a cacophony of honking horns and motorbikes buzzing between cars, buses, and tuk-tuks as people travel around the Nepalese capital. Here, at least on the surface, things seem normal.

articles.title: The Best Citrus Perfumes Are Surprisingly Versatile
articles.summary: According to experts, citrus pairs beautifully with other notes, making the best citrus fragrances by Dior, Guerlain, and more surprisingly versatile.
body: If fruity fragrances lean too sweet for your liking and clean scents feel too minimalist, citrus perfumes may be the ideal middle ground. A well-crafted citrus scent doesn’t smell like your average multisurface cleaning spray or a simple squeeze of lemon; it’s more nuanced than that.

“A fruity perfume and a citrus-forward perfume speak entirely different languages on the skin,” Guerlain perfume creation director and perfumer Delphine Jelk tells Vogue. “A fruity fragrance is about lushness, roundness, and indulgence and often leans gourmand or soft. Citrus, on the other hand, is about light, energy, and crispness. Citrus notes come from the zests—the peel—so they offer an immediate, sparkling bite, an awakening of the senses.”

Citrus notes are remarkably versatile, according to Jelk. “Citrus marries beautifully with aromatic herbs like basil, mint, or thyme, which heightens its natural green facet,” she says, noting that citrus can work just as well with unexpected pairings, such as spices. She adds that woody, ambery, and musky bases create “gorgeous tension between a bright opening and a deep, sensual dry-down.” Scroll on to discover Vogue ’s favorite citrus perfumes.
points: According to experts, citrus pairs beautifully with other notes, making the best citrus fragrances by Dior, Guerlain, and more surprisingly versatile.

articles.title: Kendall Jenner Has Her Own Kind of Romance
articles.summary: The model and face of Emporio Armani’s Power of You fragrance reflects on her first Venice Film Festival and the beauty rituals she learned from her mom.
body: It’s only Kendall Jenner’s second time in the city of Venice —and her first at the Venice Film Festival. When Vogue catches up with her, she has barely had time to settle in: she landed the previous day and will be gone again by morning. First, though, there is a dress to put on and a debut festival carpet to walk.

Venice already comes with its own rather romantic Jenner family association. Her first visit, last summer, was for a wedding, and Kylie Jenner came as her date. “It was just like we were on just a million dates together in Venice,” she remembers. “So I’d say now, Venice reminds me of Kylie, which is really sweet. It’s sisterly romance.” There are, of course, the city’s more obvious charms, too. “It’s so beautiful. It’s so unique. It’s one of a kind.”

Scent, it turns out, is also something Jenner associates with the women in her family. Fragrance is the final consideration in her everyday getting-ready routine. “At the end of getting dressed, I’m like, ‘Who am I today? What scent am I today?’” she says. “I’m a little bit of a snob about it too. I’m super picky about my scents.”
points: The model and face of Emporio Armani’s Power of You fragrance reflects on her first Venice Film Festival and the beauty rituals she learned from her mom.
